clue.text: Pass the reader will find a saver

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
a lector is one who reads aloud, especially lessons in church

explanation.surface: A mountain pass where a reader finds someone thrifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who amasses stamps, coins or the like keeps and hoards them, so is a kind of saver.

clue.text: Mark means to follow

definitions.meaning: to note or take notice of
to keep or comply with a rule or custom

explanation.definitionFit: To notice something; also to keep a law or festival by complying.

clue.text: They are packing in writing a lot about the queen

indicators.note: the word for a lot goes round the royal abbreviation

parts.note: loads means a great deal
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: People who pack written material with plenty about the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who fill vehicles or containers with goods.

clue.text: Go along with cash and new dice

parts.note: coin is money, cash

indicators.note: the letters of dice are made into something new by rearranging

explanation.surface: Agreeing to a gamble with money and fresh dice.
explanation.definitionFit: To happen together or agree, matching up with something.

clue.text: Farm-worker reading about a page with little hesitation

parts.note: RE means about or concerning
er is a brief hesitant sound

explanation.surface: A farmhand reading a page while hesitating slightly.
explanation.definitionFit: One who cuts and gathers the harvest.

clue.text: It is not mounted, no comment!

parts.note: a rider is an added comment or clause
less means without, so no comment becomes comment-less

explanation.surface: A refusal to speak about something not mounted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no comment' reads as a refusal to answer, but makes RIDER with LESS (without) after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a horse without anyone on its back.

clue.text: Level with the German about a show-off

indicators.note: the two words for level and the German go round the letter a

parts.note: par means level, as in on a par
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Someone level-headed with a German about a braggart.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who struts and displays himself ostentatiously.

clue.text: See how all may be changed without discrimination

indicators.note: the letters of the preceding words can be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Watch how everything might be altered indiscriminately.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiscriminate and on a large scale, as in mass slaughter.

clue.text: A grave message

parts.note: grave looks like 'serious', but it is the burial place: the words on a tombstone

explanation.definitionFit: Inscriptions on tombstones commemorate the dead buried beneath.

clue.text: A way a jerk is likely to move about

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
a tic is an involuntary jerk or twitch

explanation.surface: A road where a twitchy person is liable to wander.
explanation.walkthrough: An astatic needle or instrument has no fixed position, so it tends to swing around.
explanation.definitionFit: Unstable and lacking a steady orientation, as a magnetic needle unaffected by the earth's field.

clue.text: Win causing quiet churchman trouble

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
REV is short for Reverend, a clergyman
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A victory that brings a hushed clergyman some bother.
explanation.definitionFit: To triumph or come out on top is a synonym.

clue.text: A paper carrier for cheese cafes use

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

indicators.note: the letters of cafes are put to a new use, worked into a different order

explanation.surface: A case for documents that cafes employ to carry cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'use' signals rearranging CAFES into FCASE after BRIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat case for carrying documents and papers to work.

clue.text: Postures which set cans rolling

indicators.note: rolling means tumbling about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Positions that send tins tumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: Ways of standing or attitudes taken up.

clue.text: Fishermen time the waves

parts.note: rollers are long heavy waves

explanation.surface: Anglers at sea timing the breakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglers who fish by trailing a baited line behind a moving boat.

clue.text: Stopped appearing cold and relaxed

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
eased means loosened or relaxed

explanation.surface: Someone who halted looking chilly but calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Came to an end, halted: a direct synonym.

clue.text: Individual make-up

definitions.meaning: a person, especially an odd one

explanation.definitionFit: A distinctive person; also the combined qualities that form one's nature.

clue.text: Equipment for photographers wanting great pictures

definitions.text: Equipment for photographers wanting great pictures

parts.words: Equipment for photographers wanting great pictures
parts.note: great is meant literally as big: devices that make prints larger

explanation.definitionFit: Darkroom apparatus that projects a negative to make bigger prints.

clue.text: Young head, that has novelty

parts.note: new means young or fresh
a ness is a headland, a promontory

explanation.surface: A young leader who brings something fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is the geographical sense, a headland, as in place names like Loch Ness's neighbour Sheerness.
explanation.definitionFit: The quality of being fresh and original is an abstract synonym.

clue.text: Lots get knocked down here, also more get injured

indicators.note: injured means damaged, so the letters of also more are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Many people are floored here, and more are hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots' are items at auction, and 'knocked down' means sold by the auctioneer's hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: An auction room where items are sold to the highest bidder.

clue.text: Lucerne's footballers depicted in all notes

definitions.note: Lucerne's is read as lucerne is

indicators.note: the footballers are shown inside the word all

parts.note: taken as written
FA is the Football Association
fa is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: The Swiss city's soccer team portrayed in every musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lucerne' looks like the Swiss city, but it is the fodder plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucerne is another name for the forage plant also called purple medick.

clue.text: Hope to get praise?

indicators.note: the letters of praise are got into a new order, the question mark flagging the trick

explanation.surface: Wishing to be complimented.
explanation.definitionFit: To aim at or long for something is to hope for it.

clue.text: Well liked and most acceptable in the tall tree

indicators.note: the letter for acceptable is placed inside the tree

parts.note: a poplar is a tall, slender tree
U means upper-class, socially acceptable

explanation.surface: Favoured and very welcome up in a lofty tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Liked or admired by many people.

clue.text: Testing, testing!

parts.note: looks like a microphone check, but means a trial held a second time

explanation.definitionFit: A second hearing of a case in court.

clue.text: Trust concerning cut including one

parts.note: RE means about or concerning

indicators.note: the word for cut takes the numeral one within it

parts.note: to lance is to cut open, as a boil
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Faith in a matter of an incision with one person involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Dependence or confidence placed in someone is a synonym.

clue.text: Angle for credit all round a French department

indicators.note: the credit abbreviation surrounds the department

parts.note: the Orne is a department of Normandy

explanation.surface: Fishing for credit around a region of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angle' looks like fishing, but it means a corner.
explanation.definitionFit: The point where two lines or walls meet.

clue.text: He's too apt to upset a medical practitioner

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the preceding letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man so ready to cause distress to a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A therapist who treats ailments by manipulating bones and muscles.

clue.text: The man wanting payment for supplying a horse

definitions.meaning: one who bills or demands a fee

explanation.surface: Someone asking for money in return for providing a steed.
explanation.definitionFit: One who levies a fee; also a mount ridden into battle by a knight.

clue.text: Business organisation with high tone it gets the bird

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business organisation
alt means high in pitch, as in the phrase in alt

explanation.surface: A company with a lofty manner is given the bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the bird' suggests being jeered at, but 'the bird' is the definition: a small British tit.
explanation.definitionFit: A small black-and-white songbird of the tit family.

clue.text: Insist upon some being green for certain

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are used, running across them

explanation.surface: Demanding that some be environmentally friendly for sure.
explanation.definitionFit: To compel observance of a rule is to insist on it.

clue.text: Lengthy talk, in part to force a soldier to retreat

indicators.note: the reversed group goes inside the word for part

parts.note: a role is a part in a play

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so force and soldier are read in reverse

parts.note: to ram is to force
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A long speech about making a soldier fall back, as part of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retreat' turns RAM + GI into IGMAR, which goes into ROLE after its R.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, rambling and complicated account or procedure.
